title: 50 things to do before you're 11¾ (National Trust)
what_it_contains: Official page of the National Trust checklist of 50 outdoor activities for children (tick-off list, activity book, stickers).
why_relevant: Model for a '34 गांव में करने/जानने की 34 बातें' checklist; shows a simple numbered list + tick-off works at national scale.

title: Creating the long-running 50 things to do before you're 11¾ (Behaviour Change case study)
what_it_contains: Case study: launched 2012 after NT 'Natural Childhood' report; estimated 5.6 million children participated; over 90% of visitors engaging at properties in year one said they would spend more time outdoors; 170+ media pieces; mechanisms: 60-page activity book, stickers, posters, radio/newspaper ads.
why_relevant: Evidence that a printed checklist/activity book with stickers drives participation; the 90% figure is self-reported intention, not measured behaviour.

title: INTACH Heritage Education and Communication Service (HECS) brochure
what_it_contains: HECS set up 1998; Heritage Clubs in schools since 2002 (urban and rural); each member gets a Heritage Club Badge and Heritage Club Passport; teacher Heritage Education Kit (activity sheets, pledge, heritage calendar); 150+ teacher workshops; National Heritage Quiz in English, Hindi and regional languages; 'Route to Roots' (2016-17) all-India poster competition on family/community identity; FilmIt: 3000+ 2-3 minute student films; 'The Hornbill Warrior' colouring storybook on personal heritage; JAGO citizenship programme incl. Rajasthan.
why_relevant: Indian precedent for exactly the formats proposed: heritage passport + badge, activity sheets, family-identity poster competition, short student films. INTACH Heritage Club could be a partner for resettlement-village schools.

title: INTACH HECS: Heritage Clubs
what_it_contains: Heritage Club page (HTTP 503 when fetched 26 Sep 2026; search snippet: essay and painting competitions for classes 6-9, club members motivated to learn local heritage).
why_relevant: How a school joins an INTACH heritage club; human should open it to get current joining fee and kit.

title: 6 schools compete in national heritage quiz (Tribune)
what_it_contains: INTACH National Heritage Quiz 2024 described as largest school quiz in the country; district round with 80 students from 6 schools, classes 7-10.
why_relevant: Shows the quiz format is alive in 2024 and run through local INTACH chapters; a '34 गांव' round could be proposed to INTACH Bikaner chapter (existence not verified).

title: Tyneham School (TynehamVillage.org, independent guide)
what_it_contains: Tyneham (Dorset) was evacuated in 1943 for an Army live-firing range and never returned; its schoolroom was recreated in 1994 with original desks, open exercise books, nature-study books, last lesson on the blackboard with names of final pupils, coats on named pegs. Village inside Lulworth Ranges, open only on certain weekends/holidays.
why_relevant: Closest international analogue for 34 gaon for children: an army-range village where the school is the emotional centre. Thoiya pathshala still has its blackboard (frame fb2095882537884310). Supports a 'Thoiya ki pathshala' activity.

title: Tyneham Village Visitor Guide
what_it_contains: 252 residents given 28 days in November 1943; valley and 3,000 acres used as live firing range; free entry only on certain weekends and school holidays; MOD opening calendar.
why_relevant: Shows a model of limited-access days (like the Nathu Dada fair) plus an online guide with map, photos, and school page.

title: Imber New Year Open Days (Warminster Town Council)
what_it_contains: Imber village on Salisbury Plain training area (evacuated 1943, 47 days notice); only St Giles Church open to visitors on set days (29 Dec 2025-1 Jan 2026; Imberbus Day 15 Aug 2026; August bank holiday).
why_relevant: Second analogue: army-controlled lost village opened only on fixed days; the 'Imberbus' day is a family ritual comparable to the Nathu Dada fair.

title: The power of family history in adolescent identity ('Do You Know...' scale)
what_it_contains: Duke & Fivush 'Do You Know?' 20-question scale; Duke, Lazarus & Fivush (2008) Psychotherapy 45:268-272: children who knew more family history showed higher self-esteem, internal locus of control, better family functioning, lower anxiety.
why_relevant: Evidence base for 'दादा-दादी से पूछो' interview and family-tree activities; correlational (not causal) - say so.

title: Benefits of Place-based Learning: PEEC report 2010
what_it_contains: Place-based Education Evaluation Collaborative: evaluations of 10 programmes, 100+ rural/suburban/urban US schools, 2,700+ student surveys, 900+ educator surveys; reports stronger connection to place, school-community partnerships, engagement and attendance; some programmes show better test results.
why_relevant: Evidence that learning built on the child's own place increases engagement; old (2010) and US-based - use as direction, not proof for Rajasthan.

title: Heritage Schools Evaluation Research Report 2021-22 (Historic England)
what_it_contains: Evaluation of Historic England's Heritage Schools programme (local heritage in primary schools, low social-mobility areas). Search snippets: 98% of teachers said local heritage improved pupils' sense of place, 96% pride in local area, 99% belonging; ~2,500 teachers, ~2,000 primary schools, 2 million children over 10 years.
why_relevant: Strong programme-scale example of teacher training + local heritage resources; figures are teacher-reported. Historic England pages returned 403/JS-challenge to this machine.

title: Heritage Schools 10th anniversary report (Historic England news)
what_it_contains: News of 10th-anniversary impact report: learning about local heritage at school improves local pride (figures above via snippet).
why_relevant: Primary source for the Heritage Schools figures; needs a human browser.

title: National Junior Ranger Booklets (US National Park Service)
what_it_contains: Junior Ranger programmes target ages 5-14; booklets can be done in person or online; awards include printable certificate, badge, 'digital high five' or physical patch (physical reward often only in person).
why_relevant: Model for a 34 गांव 'पासपोर्ट': home/online activities earn a printable certificate; a physical stamp/badge only at the fair stall - exactly the online/in-person split needed for a closed range.

title: Evaluating a WhatsApp-based early stimulation program (Rocket Learning) - RCT registration
what_it_contains: AEA RCT registry: cluster RCT of Rocket Learning's WhatsApp parenting programme, 4,000+ households with children 0-28 months, Fatehabad and Panipat (Haryana); results not yet published.
why_relevant: Shows WhatsApp-delivered, parent-mediated learning is being run and rigorously tested in rural north India next door to Rajasthan; no outcome data yet.

title: Project SMILE facilitated education to 3.5 lakh students in Rajasthan during pandemic
what_it_contains: Rajasthan school education department's SMILE (Social Media Interface for Learning Engagement), from 13 April 2020: content sent through ~20,000 WhatsApp groups; average 3.5 lakh students daily, peak 4.56 lakh.
why_relevant: Proves Rajasthan government schools, teachers and parents already have WhatsApp group habits; 34 गांव cards can travel through the same teacher groups.

title: ASER 2024 National findings
what_it_contains: First ASER digital module (age 14-16): almost 90% have a smartphone at home; 82.2% can use one; only 27% (age 14) to 37.8% (age 16) own one; 36.2% boys vs 26.9% girls own; 57% used it for education last week. Rajasthan: 12.7% of girls 15-16 not enrolled.
why_relevant: Design rule: content must reach children through a parent's/family phone, not the child's own; girls have less access.

title: WhatsApp Terms of Service (Age clause)
what_it_contains: 'You must be at least 13 years old to register for and use our Services on your own (or such greater age required in your country)'; parent-managed accounts where available.
why_relevant: Children under 13 must not be asked to send anything on their own WhatsApp; all submissions go via a parent/teacher number.

title: DPDP Rules 2025, Rule 10: verifiable consent for processing personal data of a child
what_it_contains: Rule 10: Data Fiduciary must obtain verifiable consent of the parent before processing any personal data of a child; parent identity/age verified via details already held, voluntarily provided, or a token (e.g. DigiLocker). Status: comes into force 13 May 2027. DPDP Act 2023 s.9: child = under 18; no tracking, behavioural monitoring or targeted advertising directed at children.
why_relevant: Legal basis for the site's children's-content rules. Official gazette G.S.R. 846(E) dated 13.11.2025 should be linked from meity.gov.in (not opened here).

title: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (Wikipedia)
what_it_contains: Rules notified 13 November 2025 (G.S.R. 843-846(E)); phased: Board immediately, consent managers after 12 months, most duties (incl. Rule 10) after 18 months.
why_relevant: Timeline check for the DPDP rule citation.

title: Grandmothers to narrate tales in govt schools: boon for Rajasthan kids (Deccan Herald)
what_it_contains: Rajasthan education department order (2017): grandmothers invited once a month to the Saturday Bal Sabha for classes 1-5 to tell stories; 'no financial implications'. (Body text from search snippet; HT/PressReader 15 May 2017 has the same story.)
why_relevant: An existing government mechanism (Saturday Bal Sabha with grandmothers) into which a '34 गांव की कहानी' session fits at zero cost; check if the order is still followed in 2026.

title: Guidelines for implementation of 10 Bagless Days in schools (NCERT/PSSCIVE)
what_it_contains: NEP 2020 10 bagless days for classes 6-8: visits to places/monuments of historical and cultural importance, meeting local artists; methods include surveys, case studies and 'interviews involving community/parents'; activity 'study the history of the place'.
why_relevant: Gives teachers an official slot (bagless days) to run the 34 गांव interview and map activities in classes 6-8.

title: Missed Call Do, Kahani Suno returns! (Pratham Books)
what_it_contains: Missed-call IVR: caller gets a call back, chooses language (English, Hindi, Kannada, Marathi) and age group (<5 or >5), hears an audio story; no internet or smartphone needed; 300+ stories.
why_relevant: Proven no-internet audio model for 60-second village stories; a paid IVR is only worth it if WhatsApp voice notes fail to reach feature-phone homes.

title: StoryWeaver (Pratham Books)
what_it_contains: Open (CC BY 4.0) multilingual children's storybook platform; users can create, translate, download and print; a Marwari library was created with SNS Foundation (search snippet).
why_relevant: Free tool to publish a 34 गांव illustrated storybook (e.g. Nathu Dada, Thoiya school) in Hindi and Marwari/Rajasthani, printable for schools; CC BY means others can reuse.

title: Oral History Workshop / Citizen Historians (1947 Partition Archive)
what_it_contains: Volunteers (incl. students) attend an oral-history workshop and record one interview with a witness within a month to become Citizen Historians; interviews in the interviewee's language; 12,000+ oral histories, 1,000+ certified citizen historians.
why_relevant: Indian displacement-memory model: short training + one recorded interview per young person. Adapt for teenagers (13-17) of 34 गांव families.

title: The Great Thanksgiving Listen (StoryCorps)
what_it_contains: Annual US programme where students record interviews with elders (grandparents) using a guided app; with permission archived at the Library of Congress; age 13+; teachers use it in curriculum.
why_relevant: Template for a yearly 'दादा-दादी से पूछो' week tied to the Nathu Dada fair or Holi; age 13+ rule mirrors WhatsApp.

title: Museum on Wheels (CSMVS, Mumbai)
what_it_contains: Travelling museum bus since 2015 visiting schools in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan and others; guided tours, workshops, take-home activity sheets; free; school provides parking, power, space for 25-30 people; book 4 weeks ahead. Reported reach ~14 lakh people (press).
why_relevant: Shows 'bring the heritage to the school' when children cannot visit - the right direction for a closed range; the team version is a 1-hour school session with printed photos, not a bus.

title: Sanskriti Museums (Museum of Everyday Art etc.)
what_it_contains: Sanskriti Kendra, Anandagram (Delhi): Museum of Everyday Art (1984), Terracotta, Textiles; 'Sanskriti Yatra' school workshops.
why_relevant: The 'Museum of Everyday Art' idea fits 34 गांव: objects families carried out in 1984-87 (matka, charkha, chakki, patta) photographed as a virtual 'घर का संग्रहालय'.

title: Play with Google Arts & Culture
what_it_contains: Free browser games: Puzzle Party (jigsaws, 3 difficulty levels), Art Coloring Book (colour online or print), Pocket Gallery (AR); most need no login.
why_relevant: Formats to copy cheaply (jigsaw of a village photo, print-and-colour line art) without joining Google A&C; Google A&C partnership is not realistic for a small team.

title: JuxtaposeJS (Knight Lab)
what_it_contains: Free open-source before/after image slider; works with touch on phones; embed code or JS library (GitHub NUKnightLab/juxtapose).
why_relevant: Tool for 'तब और अब' sliders (e.g. 1955 map vs today's satellite; old family photo vs today's ruin). Needs pairs of images - old photos must come from families.

title: StoryMapJS (Knight Lab)
what_it_contains: Free tool to tell a story as a sequence of places on a map or on a large image (e.g. a historic map).
why_relevant: Could run a 'नाथू दादा के 12 गांव' or 'कुम्भाणा से रामनगर' story map over the 1955 AMS sheet; but adds JS weight - a static SVG sequence may be lighter.

title: Pannellum 360 panorama viewer
what_it_contains: Free, open-source, lightweight, plug-in free HTML5/WebGL panorama viewer.
why_relevant: If families ever get Army permission to shoot a 360 photo on fair day, this displays it with no licence cost. Otherwise 360/AR is not realistic here.

title: List of commissioned community radio stations as on 03.12.2025 (MIB)
what_it_contains: MIB list: 40+ Rajasthan entries; none in Bikaner district. Nearest: Chetna Radio (Sangaria, Hanumangarh) and 'Mastii' (Sriganganagar). (PDF contains station contacts; not stored locally for privacy.)
why_relevant: Community radio is not a realistic channel for resettlement villages in Chhatargarh/Khajuwala/Kolayat (a CRS covers ~10-15 km). Radio route = Akashvani Bikaner (not verified here).

title: Mobile Vaani: a voice-based community media network (Gram Vaani, IIT Delhi)
what_it_contains: IVR platform: people call a number to record/listen to local-dialect voice messages; networks in Jharkhand/Bihar/MP and with 30+ community radios incl. Rajasthan.
why_relevant: Voice-first, dialect-first model (Bagri) for elders' stories; cost unknown - a paid service is probably too much for a volunteer team; WhatsApp voice notes do most of this for free.

title: Backgrounder: The Drone Rules, 2021 (PIB)
what_it_contains: Red zone = 'no-drone zone' where operation is permitted only by the Central Government; nano drones <=250 g; operators must check the Digital Sky airspace map.
why_relevant: Any drone/360 aerial shooting over the range for a 'virtual tour' needs central permission; team must not commission or re-publish new drone footage of the range for children's content.

title: The Official Secrets Act, 1923 (Indian Kanoon)
what_it_contains: s.2 'sketch' includes any photograph; 'prohibited place' includes military establishments/camps; s.3 penalises approaching or photographing a prohibited place for purposes prejudicial to the State.
why_relevant: Children's activities must never ask kids or families to photograph Army camps/equipment; use only village ruins, shrines and water bodies already filmed publicly.

title: Ethical reporting guidelines (UNICEF)
what_it_contains: Principles: dignity and rights of every child, privacy and confidentiality, best interests over advocacy; change name/obscure identity of internally displaced or at-risk children where harm possible.
why_relevant: Basis for the site's child-content rules (children of displaced families).

title: NCPCR media guidelines for children (copy)
what_it_contains: Copy of NCPCR guidelines on media and children (not read in this session).
why_relevant: Indian reference to read before publishing any child's image/voice.

title: Bagri language
what_it_contains: Bagri (ISO 639-3 bgq), Rajasthani group; mainly Sriganganagar and Hanumangarh, small population in Churu and Bikaner; ~1.89 million speakers in India. SIL sociolinguistic survey 2011 exists (https://www.sil.org/resources/archives/43105).
why_relevant: Resettlement chaks in Khajuwala/Chhatargarh lie in the Bagri/Marwari zone; audio in the elders' own speech (not standard Hindi) is the point; no written Bagri children's material found.

title: Improving Children's Cultural Heritage Experience Using Game-based Learning at a Living Museum
what_it_contains: Mobile scavenger hunt at Sarawak Cultural Village: children in the mobile-game group reported higher emotional connection than the pamphlet group (per search summary).
why_relevant: Evidence that quest/treasure-hunt formats help engagement; but another study found children preferred entertainment over deep learning - keep quests short and tied to one fact.

title: The Ocean Game: children's engagement and learning with a treasure-hunt game
what_it_contains: 46 children aged 6-12: mobile treasure-hunt players interacted more with exhibits and retained more details than paper-version users (per search summary).
why_relevant: Supports photo-based 'खोजो' quests; small sample, museum setting.

title: Guidance in museum virtual tours: impact of a gamified mobile guide on elementary students
what_it_contains: Gamified mobile guide with immediate feedback supported elementary students' knowledge and satisfaction in virtual museum tours better than a text-based paper guide (per search summary).
why_relevant: Recent evidence for virtual tours with quiz feedback - relevant because 34 gaon can only be toured virtually.

title: DCH Bikaner 1981 Part XIII-A&B: amenities of the 29 inhabited range villages (re-read for children's activities)
what_it_contains: Amenity codes re-read from the repo CSV (OCR, confidence medium): drinking water W (well) in 28 of 29 villages, TK (tank) in 25, tap (T) only in Rampura, Jagatsinghpura, Khanisar, Kumbhasar, tube well in Kanolai and Kumbhana, canal in none; primary school (P) listed in 23 of 29; middle school in Kumbhana and Motolai.
why_relevant: Real data for the 'पानी जासूस' and 'हमारे गांव का स्कूल' activities (maths + environment).
